title: Gateway Lunar Space Station Architecture
sourceTitle: NASA Gateway Program - Deep Space Outpost
summary: Gateway is humanity's first lunar-orbiting space station, established under the NASA Artemis program in collaboration with international partners (ESA, JAXA, CSA, MBRSC).
facts: Gateway operates in a Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) around the Moon, providing continuous line-of-sight to Earth and access to the lunar South Pole.
The station serves as a multi-purpose staging hub for Artemis lunar surface expeditions and future deep space missions to Mars.
Initial configurations support up to four crew members for 30-to-90 day habitation stints with autonomous robotics operations during uncrewed periods.
Power and Propulsion Element (PPE) delivers 60 kW solar electric propulsion (SEP) for orbital maneuvers and stationkeeping.

title: HALO Pressurized Cabin & Life Support Architecture
sourceTitle: NASA Habitation and Logistics Outpost (HALO) Specifications
summary: HALO is the initial pressurized habitat and command center for astronauts visiting Gateway, providing living quarters, scientific research interfaces, and docking ports.
facts: HALO is manufactured by Northrop Grumman based on the flight-proven Cygnus spacecraft architecture.
Provides command, control, life support distribution, and data handling for the initial Gateway configuration.
Features multiple International Standard Payload Racks (ISPR) and external payload attachment fixtures for heliophysics and space biology research.
Equipped with the Canadian Space Agency Canadarm3 robotic interface for external maintenance and cargo transfer.

title: Lunar International Habitat Specifications
summary: Lunar I-Hab is the primary deep-space living and scientific habitat module provided by ESA with environmental life support contributions from JAXA.
facts: Provides approximately 10 cubic meters of usable pressurized living volume per astronaut.
Integrates advanced closed-loop Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) with high-efficiency carbon dioxide scrubbing and trace contaminant control.
Incorporates microgravity crew sleep quarters, circadian lighting regulation, and modular countermeasure workout stations.
Equipped with optical and sensor ports for deep-space autonomous navigation and radiation dosimetry.

title: Orion Deep Space Human Exploration Vehicle
sourceTitle: NASA Orion Spacecraft Overview & Artemis Missions
summary: Orion is NASA's exploration-class spacecraft designed to transport astronauts beyond low-Earth orbit to the Moon and return them safely through lunar-velocity atmospheric reentry.
facts: Crew Module accommodates 4 astronauts for up to 21 days autonomous flight (extended to months when docked with Gateway).
European Service Module (ESM) provided by ESA powers the spacecraft with 4 solar arrays, propellant, water, and breathable atmosphere.
Features a 5-meter diameter ablative Avcoat heat shield designed to withstand 5,000°F (2,760°C) during 25,000 mph lunar atmospheric entry.
Autonomous flight guidance and optical hazard detection computers ensure crew return even during complete ground loss.

title: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Exercise & Circadian Countermeasures
sourceTitle: NASA Human Research Program - Spaceflight Countermeasures
summary: NASA protocols for preserving astronaut musculoskeletal density, cardiovascular health, and circadian rhythms during long-duration deep-space transit.
facts: Astronauts perform a mandatory minimum of 2 hours daily physical countermeasures combining resistive (ARED) and aerobic (T2 cycle/treadmill) workouts.
Microgravity without countermeasure leads to 1-1.5% bone mineral density loss per month in weight-bearing bones.
Autonomous optical monitoring of crew kinematics helps verify exercise posture compliance and detect early musculoskeletal fatigue.
Circadian lighting protocols (dynamic blue-enriched morning light and red-shifted evening light) synchronize crew rest-work cycles.
